instruction: Generate an automatically updating table of contents for the thesis according to the specifications in the “Graduation Thesis Requirements” document, and modify all formatting throughout the thesis as required.

dim1: The delivered file is in .docx format and can be opened normally.
The body content of the delivered Word document is not composed of full-page images.
dim2: +5: Automatically updating table of contents: The table of contents is a Word automatic TOC field or an updateable TOC object; its page numbers can be refreshed by updating the field; it is not ordinary manually typed text or a screenshot.
+3: A table-of-contents page appears in the document.

+5: TOC heading levels: The table of contents includes level-one and level-two headings; level-one headings use the ordering format “Part One, Part Two, Part Three”; level-two headings use the ordering format “One, Two, Three.”

+3: Core TOC entries: The table of contents includes the following level-one headings: “List of Chinese and English Abbreviations,” “Foreword,” “Part One: Construction of a Multimodal Rehabilitation Database,” “Part Two: Response Characteristics of Integrated Traditional Chinese Medicine Intervention,” “Part Three: Development and Interpretation of an Efficacy Prediction Model,” “Discussion,” “Conclusion,” and “References.”
+3: TOC content and heading formatting: All TOC entries use SimHei in Chinese font size No. 4; page numbers appear to the right of the TOC entries.
+3: Page-number settings: The cover page does not display a page number; the table-of-contents page does not display a page number.
+3: Page-number settings: The Chinese Abstract and English Abstract pages use Roman-numeral page numbers.
+3: Beginning with the “List of Chinese and English Abbreviations” page (the page after the table of contents), the thesis restarts page numbering at 1 and uses Arabic-numeral page numbers.
+3: Page-number format: Page numbers are uniformly centered at the bottom of the page.
+3: Page margins: The margins throughout the document are 2.5 cm top, 2.5 cm bottom, 3.0 cm left, and 2.5 cm right.
+3: References font: In every entry, Chinese text uses SimSun in Chinese font size Small No. 4; English text and numbers use Times New Roman in Chinese font size Small No. 4.
+3: References numbering: Reference-list numbers use Arabic numerals enclosed in English square brackets, such as “[1]” and “[2].”
+3: Reference-entry paragraph formatting meets the following requirements: numbers are left-aligned, line spacing is 1.5 lines, and text has a hanging indent of 2 characters.
+1: The thesis title on the cover page uses KaiTi in Chinese font size Small No. 2.

+5: The college name, discipline and major, degree category, author name, supervisor, and completion date on the cover page use KaiTi in Chinese font size Small No. 2; English text, numbers, and letters use Times New Roman in Chinese font size Small No. 2.

+3: The content on the right side of the Chinese Abstract page is divided into sections labeled “[Objective],” “[Methods],” “[Results],” and “[Conclusion]”; except for numbers and English letters, all text uses unbolded SimSun in Chinese font size Small No. 4.
+1: On the Chinese Abstract page, “Keywords” uses SimHei in Chinese font size No. 4, and the content following “Keywords” uses SimSun in Chinese font size Small No. 4.

+5: All tables are presented as three-line tables (standard three-line table widths: top and bottom borders: 1.5 pt [thick lines]; column-rule line [the line below the header]: 0.75 pt [thin line]), with no vertical lines and no intermediate horizontal lines.
+3: Level-two headings use SimHei in Chinese font size Small No. 4.

+5: Text formatting within tables: Chinese text uses SimSun; English text/numbers use Times New Roman; the table header (column-heading row) uses Chinese font size No. 5 and is bold; the table body (data rows) uses Chinese font size Small No. 5.
-3: Footer text other than page numbers appears anywhere in the document.
-3: Page numbers overlap the body text, footnotes, figures, or tables.

-5: In-text reference citation numbers do not meet the following requirements: citation numbers in the body text are enclosed in square brackets; citation numbers in the body text are displayed as superscripts; the numbers use Arabic numerals enclosed in English square brackets, such as “[1]” and “[2].”
